did.abstract: Collection contains production materials, administrative records, press and promotional materials, and correspondence from late 1970s San Francisco punk zine Search & Destroy and subcultural publishing outfit RE/Search Publications (briefly V/Search Publications). Established in 1981, RE/Search documents underground trends including body modification, industrial culture, and zines, as well as countercultural literary figures such as J. G. Ballard and William S. Burroughs. Material represented in this collection was accumulated by San Francisco-based publisher, writer, musician, and artist V. Vale.

bioghist.head: Biography/History
bioghist.p: V. Vale, born Vale Hamanaka, is an influential independent publisher in San Francisco who brought the eccentricities and personalities of punk, underground, and alternative culture to greater public prominence. He was born in 1944 in a Japanese internment camp in Jerome, Arkansas to the actor Conrad Yama (Kiyoshi Conrad Hamanaka) and Mary Takaoka of the vaudeville trio the Taka Sisters. Vale later studied English at the University of California, Berkeley, and attended a semester of graduate studies at San Francisco State University before he went on to become one of the early members of the rock/metal band Blue Cheer (1967).

In the early 1970s, Vale obtained a position as a mail-order clerk at San Francisco's independent bookstore-publisher City Lights. There, he befriended some of the prominent figures of the 1950s Beat Generation, namely Lawrence Ferlinghetti and Allen Ginsberg. In 1977, with support from Ferlinghetti, Ginsberg, and a doctor friend, Vale gathered funding to produce the tabloid-like publication Search and Destroy. Vale sought to document San Francisco's burgeoning punk scene and to re-contextualize its image from the one presented by mainstream media. Emulating the editorial aesthetics of Andy Warhol's Interview, Search and Destroy featured seminal DIY artists and punk rock musicians such as the Ramones and the Weirdos at San Francisco venues like the Mabuhay Gardens and Deaf Club. Vale also made occasional contributions to other punk rock and underground periodicals/zines including Slash and Another Room.

Vale met Andrea Juno in May 1980, and the pair went on to produce a number of works under RE/Search Publications, abandoning the title Search and Destroy as the punk scene garnered increasing popularity. Through monetary support by Geoff Travis of Rough Trade Records, the two produced RE/Search #1-3, which maintained much of the same stylistic features and tabloid-like format as Search and Destroy. In 1981, they created the commercial typesetting business RE/Search Typography, to gain greater financial and editorial liberty for their publications. In 1982, Vale and Juno produced their first book, RE/Search #4-5, focusing on the works and insights of William S. Burroughs, Genesis P-Orridge of Throbbing Gristle, and Brion Gysin. Subsequent projects had similarly centralized themes.

The partnership between Juno and Vale led to the publication of more than 20 books, including works by J.G. Ballard, Daniel P. Mannix, and Octave Mirbeau, among others. Modern Primitives, Pranks, and Incredibly Strange Films are some of their most notable publications. Following a period of administrative disagreement where RE/Search Publications was briefly relocated to New York, Juno and Vale dissolved the company in late 1995. Andrea Juno went on to start Juno Books, and Vale began publishing under V/Search, although he continues to use the RE/Search brand.

Following the split, Vale started working with his current partner, filmmaker and documentarian Marian Wallace at his same studio in the North Beach neighborhood of San Francicsco. Along with continuing to publish magazines and books, the two started a monthly, hour-long interview program on cable TV titled The Counter Culture Hour in 2005.
Vale periodically gives lectures at various universities and is a frequent panelist at art and zine festivals. Vale and Marian Wallace have one daughter named Valentine.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: This collection is comprised of production materials, both paper-based and digital; administrative records; personal materials; and press and promotional materials for Search and Destroy, RE/Search Publications, and V/Search Publications, accumulated and stored by independent publisher V. Vale in San Francisco. It also contains a significant amount of correspondence, gifts, and project proposals that were sent to RE/Search Publications during the 1990s, illustrating the breadth and interest in local and international subcultures. It is important to note that the collection does not contain production or administrative material for every title produced by RE/Search or V/Search, nor does it contain a back catalog of the final works themselves. The majority of the content related to the publications exists in the form of proofs, layouts, manuscript edits, interview transcripts, and research subject files, providing valuable insight into the production process. Administrative and business related materials include financial records, lawsuit settlements, invoices, and business consultation materials for RE/Search Publications and RE/Search Typography, as well as those for smaller ventures (e.g. RE/Shirts). The collection also contains a rich selection of underground and alternative publications, including books, zines, comics, and periodicals, as well as audiovisual materials collected by Vale, representing subjects ranging from Beat poetry to punk and sadomasochism. A small amount of Vale's personal correspondence, ephemera, and memorabilia are also included.

The digital files were created by V. Vale and Marian Wallace between 1988 and 2010 and have content related to RE/Search Publications business operations and RE/Search and V/Search publishing projects. The files contain backups of RE/Search Publications office computers, which include born-digital materials such as digital images, photographs, videos, designs, layouts, and manuscripts from many RE/Search and V/Search book and zine publishing projects; software programs; RE/Search email accounts and correspondence that pertain to RE/Search publishing projects; RE/Search website designs and user reports; address and phone books; promotional materials; and V. Vale and Marian Wallace's personal files. Some scans of paper materials are included in the collection of digital files.

The majority of the digital files were created on a Mac computer using HFS file systems and saved onto 112 optical disks, nineteen SyQuest drives, and thirteen floppy disks, while some were created on a PC with FAT12 and FAT13 file systems and saved onto six floppy disks. Original file formats include .WPD, .EPS, .DOC, .QUARK, .PSD, .TIFF, .AVI, .HTML, .MIM, .MPEG, .TXT, .RTF, .AI, .XLSX, .MBMP, and .PNG.

bioghist.head: Biography/History
bioghist.p: Search and Destroy was a punk zine published between 1977 and 1979 in San Francisco, where it was initiated by editor V. Vale during his time working as a mail clerk at City Lights bookstore. A large group of correspondents, contributors, and staff from all over the United States and Europe worked (often pseudonymously) to run, publish, distribute, and create content for the zine, which aimed to document the burgeoning punk movement. Although local Bay Area bands and venues were featured prominently, content included interviews with bands and artists such as the Ramones, Devo, Talking Heads, and Joe Strummer, articles on punk music and politics, international directories of bands and magazines, and street reports on events everywhere from Seattle to London. The publication also showcased striking graphics and photography, much of which was original work supplied by photographers Ruby Ray, Kamera Zie, Bruce Conner, and Richard Peterson.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Series 1 contains materials related to the production and publication of Search and Destroy and two related projects, the unpublished Search and Destroy: Photographs and Search and Destroy: The Complete Reprint. In addition to original issues of Search and Destroy, the layouts, collages, administrative records, and proofs included here help to illustrate physical production and distribution of the zine, while the drafts of articles and interviews, photographs, notes, research and correspondence offer insight into the creative process, as well as previously unpublished material. Finally, this series also contains a large collection of punk related flyers, posters, periodicals and zines that extends beyond the specific scope and span of the zine itself.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains the notes, articles, photographs, research files, and other materials that constituted the collaborative labor and intellectual content of Search and Destroy. Notable zine content includes handwritten and annotated interviews with Bay Area and Southern California punk bands such as The Nuns, the Screamers, The Avengers, and X, as well as artists such as Steve Jones, Devo, The Clash, and The Ramones. The majority of the material is found in the Subject Files, which cover certain staff and regular contributors such as Nico Ordway, Caffeine Jean, Ruby Ray, and Kamera Zie, in addition to numerous other bands, artists, publications and venues relevant to the punk rock scene. While some files contain interviews, collected articles, photographs and 7 inch records, many contain only a few clippings. As with the interviews, Bay Area and Southern California bands and venues received a more complete treatment, as did artists and individuals such as Iggy Pop and Sid Vicious. The notes cover a wide range of topics, from brainstorming on the fundamental principles and aesthetics of Search and Destroy to lists of potential contributors.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: While still relevant to the production of Search and Destroy, this subseries contains material that extends beyond the scope and span of the magazine itself. Dating to the late 1970s and early 1980s, this collection of ephemera, periodicals, and zines provides insight into the punk rock scene from both a local and a global perspective. Ephemera includes press kits and releases, record catalogs, and a large collection of flyers and posters that feature Bay Area and Los Angeles venues, in particular Mabuhay Gardens, and advertise for bands and local events such as Rock Against Racism and Benefit for the Coal Miner's Strike. The periodicals cover both politics and music and range from clippings to complete issues of newspapers and magazines, including publications such as Class Struggle, Worker's Vanguard, and several years' worth of Sounds, NME, and Melody Maker. Finally, the collection offers a unique and sizable selection of zines from all over the United States and the world, and includes numerous issues from influential publications such as Damage, Flipside, NoMag, Punk, Slash, Sniffin' Glue, and Ripped and Torn.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: This series contains all correspondence that did not deal directly with the administration of Search and Destroy or its consequent projects, including fan-mail, inquiries from aspiring zine makers, criticism, and mail orders from individuals. The correspondence offers a wide variety of personal communications from around the world. Because Search and Destroy solicited reports on local punk rock scenes for its recurring "Street Report" segment, correspondents often included descriptions of their local scene, even with the most routine requests. Also notable are the exchanges between contributors and staff, which contain original photos, notes, and drafts of articles and interviews.

bioghist.head: Biography/History
bioghist.p: RE/Search Publications was established in 1981 by Andrea Juno and V. Vale, former editor of Search and Destroy. Although they also published works such as Brion Gysin's Here to Go, J.G. Ballard's Atrocity Exhibition, and Octave Mirbeau's Torture Garden, RE/Search Publications is primarily known for its original works, which were largely interview based and centered on topics relating to alternative lifestyles and subcultures. Among these original works were titles such as the Industrial Culture Handbook, Pranks, Incredibly Strange Films, Modern Primitives, and Angry Women. In 1995 the partnership between Juno and Vale came to an acrimonious end, at which time Juno departed to found Juno Books in New York while Vale remained in San Francisco, publishing under the name V/Search Publications with his new partner Marion Wallace.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Series 2 contains material related to the titles produced by partners Andrea Juno and V. Vale under the name RE/Search Publications during the years 1981 to 1995. The amount and type of material found in this collection varies considerably for each title, but the available material provides insight into editorial processes, research and interview preparation, distribution of labor, and the impact of technological change on a small publisher. Material includes correspondence, original layouts, photographs, interview tapes and transcripts in various stages of editing, proofs and collected research. Collection contains no copy of RE/Search #1, no material related to RE/Search #2 and RE/Search #3, and limited material related to RE/Search #4/5 and RE/Search #6/7. Also included are correspondence and interview transcripts for the title Angry Women in Rock, which was produced and published by Andrea Juno shortly after the dissolution of their partnership.

bioghist.p: Although the character of the work changed under the oversight of Vale, Wallace, and east coast collaborator Chris Trela, V/Search Publications adopted the same approach and aesthetic as RE/Search Publications, eventually re-appropriating the name RE/Search in 1997. Material includes correspondence, original layouts, photographs, interview tapes and transcripts in various stages of editing, proofs and collected research. scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains submissions and proposals sent to RE/Search, in the form of typescripts, book proposals, sample chapters, outlines, writing samples, poetry, artwork, photographs, illustrations, drawings, music, and invitations to collaborate on literary or publishing projects. Materials span the years 1980-2010. This subseries is rich in its variety of content, since RE/Search had become known for publishing on the fringe and explicit topics, and hence attracted submissions not suited for conventional publishing houses. Although the vast majority of the submissions were not accepted by RE/Search for publication, some went on to be published elsewhere. Of note are submissions of poetry by G. Sutton Breiding, the typescript of Unfictions by Jason Price Everett, the typescript Addict with photography by Chris Keeley, the typescript of a dissertation by theatre/performance artist and writer Julie Wilson (now Wilson-Bokowiec) on Hermann Nitsch and Genesis P-Orridge, a typescript by Jaz Coleman (Killing Joke), prose and poetry submissions by Marty Wilson-Piper (The Church), a book proposal by Veronica Vera, the typescript of Whore Carnival by Shannon Bell, and a number of other proposals and typescripts relating to pornography, sex workers, and erotica. A number of submissions and proposals were sent from other countries to RE/Search.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains the subject files once housed in Vale's filing cabinets regarding a variety of topics such as art, film, and opera, usually in the form of magazines, clippings, pamphlets, cassettes, or flyers. There is also a significant amount of content for certain more esoteric topics like the parody religion Church of the Subgenius founded by J. R. "Rob" Dobbs, the First National Church of the Exquisite Panic founded by Robert Delford Brown, and the musical/visual art project Autopsia. Of particular interest might be the files regarding underground industrial bands such as Einstürzende Neubauten, Monte Cazazza, and S.P.K., as well as the feminist punk movement RiotGrrrl. scopecontent.p: This subseries contains a physically expansive and thematically diverse collection of V. Vale's periodicals, præsumably both for leisurely and research-related purposes. The largest category is "Music" which includes cultural and topical periodicals (Rock Scene, Creem, Trouser Press, etc.) as well as audio technology/production guides (Keyboard, Electronic Musician, Sound on Sound, etc.). Magazines come from sources as mainstream as the science and technology magazine Wired to those with niche audiences like the German body suspension magazine Expand. Of particular research value might be the four issues of the 1960s psychedelic periodical SF Oracle. The "Lifestyle" category contains materials related to fashion, dining, and local news. There is also a sizable amount of satirical magazines from the 1970s-1990s featuring title such as Spy and National Lampoon, and a collection of serial fiction publications from the late 1920s-1950s and 1980s – Argosy and Armchair Detective, in particular. Periodicals categorized as "International" were written in different languages. Note that while periodicals have been placed under their own discrete, categorical subheadings, many periodicals cover overlapping subjects and could fall under a different category. May contain some zine titles.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Terry Hammer runs independent record label Hammer Productions, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. Boxes 409, 410, and 417 contain eighty-five audio cassettes featuring his recordings and mixes of live performances at the Mabuhay Gardens, Old Waldorf, the Savoy Tivoli, and Berkeley Square during 1979-1980. Hammer produced these tapes for circulation on SF Bay Area radio stations, including KALX, KSAN, KSJO, and KUSF. The majority of the artists in this collection fall under the punk-rock genre, although some blues musicians like Charlie Musselwhite are also featured. Artists with comparatively greater representation in this collection include English punk band 999, the Mutants, the Offs, and Jamaican reggae singer Earl Zero. Items are arranged alphabetically by artist name.
Box 510 contains four 12" inch records featuring works from the Allies, the Saucers, and The Lewd at the Mabuhay Gardens in 1980, all recorded, mixed, and produced by Terry Hammer.
Box 511 contains five CDs of live recording mixes of The Offs, Young Canadians, and Delta 5.

bioghist.p: Vermilion Sands, née Sylvia Thornton, was an editor for Search and Destroy and member of punk bands Vermilion and the Aces and Dick Envy. She was briefly married to Vale in the 1970s. scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: This series contains digital media from various RE/Search and V/Search titles that were stored separately from their individual projects. Includes Jaz drives, SyQuest disks, 3.5 inch floppy disks, DVD-Rs and CD-Rs. V/Search publications refers to titles produced by V. Vale and Marion Wallace after the departure of Andrea Juno, from 1995-2013. Although Vale continued to affiliate himself with RE/Search Publications after the dissolution of the partnership, both reprints and new titles were published under V/Search Publications from 1995-1997, at which time the name RE/Search Publications was fully re-appropriated.

The digital files were created by V Vale and Marian Wallace between 1988 and 2010. The majority of the files are backups of born-digital materials such as digital images, photographs, videos, designs, layouts, writings, phone and address books, and software programs from RE/Search Publications office computers and RE/Search email accounts and correspondence that pertain to RE/Search publishing projects, administrative materials, and V Vale and Marian Wallace's personal files. Some digital scans of paper materials are included in the collection of digital files. Dates for each record were determined and assigned based on the dates that files were last modified, according to the file explorer.

The majority of the digital files were created on a Mac computer using HFS file systems and transferred onto 112 optical disks, nineteen SyQuest disks, and thirteen floppy disks while some were created on a PC with FAT12 and FAT13 file systems and burned onto six floppy disks. Original file formats include .wpd, .eps, .doc, .quark, .psd, .tiff, .avi, .html, .mim, .mpeg, .txt, .rtf, .ai, .xlsx, .bmp, .png.

Box 296 contains seventeen SyQuest disks with material related to V/Search Publications projects, such as the Sue Brisk project, Step Right Up! Memoirs of a Sword Swallower by Daniel P. Mannix, Zines! Vol. 1, and Search and Destroy project files; Box 315 contains seventy-three CD-Rs and nine DVD-Rs with material related to the Sue Brisk project, Modern Pagans, Robert Delford Brown, Real Conversations 1 and 2, Leary on Drugs, Punk 77; Box 24 contains four 7 inch vinyl records that were submitted to RE/Search Publications by punk bands, twenty-nine CD-Rs and one 3.5 inch floppy disk with administrative material, publishing project materials, and RE/Search Publications office computers and email backups; Box 449 contains twenty 3.5 inch floppy disks with material related to V/Search Publications projects: Zines!
